audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 16, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Ziba's provisions and untested accusation, Mephibosheth's disability and transport dependence, immediate property seizure, Shimei's protest and violence, Abishai's execution demand, David's restraint and providence interpretation, exhaustion, Hushai's espionage, Ahithophel's counsel, and public sexual seizure of ten concubines.

verses.restored: David passed a little beyond summit. Look, Ziba servant of Mephibosheth met him with pair of saddled donkeys, two hundred loaves, one hundred raisin clusters, one hundred summer-fruit portions, and skin of wine.

familiar.text: And when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

modern.text: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

original.text: וְדָוִ֗ד עָבַ֤ר מְעַט֙ מֵֽהָרֹ֔אשׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה צִיבָ֛א נַ֥עַר מְפִי בֹ֖שֶׁת לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וְצֶ֨מֶד חֲמֹרִ֜ים חֲבֻשִׁ֗ים וַעֲלֵיהֶם֩ מָאתַ֨יִם לֶ֜חֶם וּמֵאָ֧ה צִמּוּקִ֛ים וּמֵ֥אָה קַ֖יִץ וְנֵ֥בֶל יָֽיִן

verses.restored: King said to Ziba, What are these for you? Ziba said, Donkeys are for household of king to ride; bread and summer fruit for young men to eat; wine for the faint in wilderness to drink.

familiar.text: And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses be for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.

modern.text: “Why do you have these?” asked the king. Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל צִיבָ֖א מָה אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר צִ֠יבָא הַחֲמוֹרִ֨ים לְבֵית הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לִרְכֹּ֗ב ולהלחם וְהַקַּ֨יִץ֙ לֶאֱכ֣וֹל הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְהַיַּ֕יִן לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת הַיָּעֵ֖ף בַּמִּדְבָּֽר

verses.restored: King said, Where is son of your master? Ziba said to king, Look, he remains in Jerusalem, because he said, Today house of Israel will return kingdom of my father to me.

familiar.text: And the king said, And where is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.

modern.text: “Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king. And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאַיֵּ֖ה בֶּן אֲדֹנֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִיבָ֜א אֶל הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הִנֵּה֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר הַיּ֗וֹם יָשִׁ֤יבוּ לִי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת מַמְלְכ֥וּת אָבִֽי

verses.restored: King said to Ziba, Look, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours. Ziba said, I bow; let me find favor in your eyes, my lord king.

familiar.text: Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.

modern.text: So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” “I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!” Shimei Curses David

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְצִבָ֔א הִנֵּ֣ה לְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִמְפִי בֹ֑שֶׁת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ הִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֔יתִי אֶמְצָא חֵ֥ן בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: King David came to Bahurim. Look, from there came a man from clan of house of Saul, whose name was Shimei son of Gera. He came out, cursing as he came.

familiar.text: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.

modern.text: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.

original.text: וּבָ֛א הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖ד עַד בַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשָּׁם֩ אִ֨ישׁ יוֹצֵ֜א מִמִּשְׁפַּ֣חַת בֵּית שָׁא֗וּל וּשְׁמוֹ֙ שִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן גֵּרָ֔א יֹצֵ֥א יָצ֖וֹא וּמְקַלֵּֽל

verses.restored: He threw stones at David and all servants of king David, though all people and all mighty warriors were at his right and left.

familiar.text: And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.

modern.text: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.

original.text: וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ אֶת דָּוִ֔ד וְאֶת כָּל עַבְדֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וְכָל הָעָם֙ וְכָל הַגִּבֹּרִ֔ים מִימִינ֖וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֽוֹ

verses.restored: Thus Shimei said in his cursing: Go out, go out, man of blood and worthless man.

familiar.text: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:

modern.text: And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!

original.text: וְכֹֽה אָמַ֥ר שִׁמְעִ֖י בְּקַֽלְל֑וֹ צֵ֥א צֵ֛א אִ֥ישׁ הַדָּמִ֖ים וְאִ֥ישׁ הַבְּלִיָּֽעַל

verses.restored: YHWH has returned upon you all blood of house of Saul, in whose place you reigned. YHWH has given kingdom into hand of Absalom your son. Look, you are in your evil, because you are a man of blood.

familiar.text: The LORD hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the LORD hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou art taken in thy mischief, because thou art a bloody man.

modern.text: The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”

original.text: הֵשִׁיב֩ עָלֶ֨יךָ יְהוָ֜ה כֹּ֣ל דְּמֵ֣י בֵית שָׁא֗וּל אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַ֨כְתָּ֙ תחתו וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ אֶת הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בְּנֶ֑ךָ וְהִנְּךָ֙ בְּרָ֣עָתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ דָּמִ֖ים אָֽתָּה

verses.restored: Abishai son of Zeruiah said to king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord king? Please let me cross and remove his head.

familiar.text: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.

modern.text: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן צְרוּיָה֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֣מָּה יְקַלֵּ֞ל הַכֶּ֤לֶב הַמֵּת֙ הַזֶּ֔ה אֶת אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אֶעְבְּרָה נָּ֖א וְאָסִ֥ירָה אֶת רֹאשֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: King said, What is there to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah? If he curses because YHWH said to him, Curse David, who can say, Why did you do so?

familiar.text: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

modern.text: But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַה לִּ֥י וְלָכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י צְרֻיָ֑ה כי יְקַלֵּ֗ל וכי יְהוָה֙ אָ֤מַר לוֹ֙ קַלֵּ֣ל אֶת דָּוִ֔ד וּמִ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ עָשִׂ֥יתָה כֵּֽן

verses.restored: David said to Abishai and all his servants, Look, my son who came from my body seeks my life; how much more now this Benjaminite. Leave him, and let him curse, because YHWH has told him.

familiar.text: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD hath bidden him.

modern.text: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the LORD has told him so.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤ד אֶל אֲבִישַׁי֙ וְאֶל כָּל עֲבָדָ֔יו הִנֵּ֥ה בְנִ֛י אֲשֶׁר יָצָ֥א מִמֵּעַ֖י מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת נַפְשִׁ֑י וְאַ֨ף כִּֽי עַתָּ֜ה בֶּן הַיְמִינִ֗י הַנִּ֤חוּ לוֹ֙ וִֽיקַלֵּ֔ל כִּ֥י אָֽמַר ל֖וֹ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Perhaps YHWH will see my affliction/eye, and YHWH will return good to me in place of his curse this day.

familiar.text: It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day.

modern.text: Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”

original.text: אוּלַ֛י יִרְאֶ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בעוני וְהֵשִׁ֨יב יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ טוֹבָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת קִלְלָת֖וֹ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: David and his men went on road. Shimei went along side of hill opposite him, cursing as he went, throwing stones alongside him and throwing dust.

familiar.text: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill’s side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.

modern.text: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.

original.text: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֖יו בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְשִׁמְעִ֡י הֹלֵךְ֩ בְּצֵ֨לַע הָהָ֜ר לְעֻמָּת֗וֹ הָלוֹךְ֙ וַיְקַלֵּ֔ל וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ לְעֻמָּת֔וֹ וְעִפַּ֖ר בֶּעָפָֽר

verses.restored: King and all people with him came exhausted, and they refreshed themselves there.

familiar.text: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.

modern.text: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself. The Counsel of Ahithophel and Hushai

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֖וֹ עֲיֵפִ֑ים וַיִּנָּפֵ֖שׁ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Absalom and all people, men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

familiar.text: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

modern.text: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

original.text: וְאַבְשָׁל֗וֹם וְכָל הָעָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֖אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: When Hushai the Archite, companion of David, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, May king live; may king live.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.

modern.text: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר בָּ֞א חוּשַׁ֧י הָאַרְכִּ֛י רֵעֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד אֶל אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חוּשַׁי֙ אֶל אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם יְחִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Absalom said to Hushai, Is this your covenant-kindness with your companion? Why did you not go with your companion?

familiar.text: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?

modern.text: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל חוּשַׁ֔י זֶ֥ה חַסְדְּךָ֖ אֶת רֵעֶ֑ךָ לָ֥מָּה לֹֽא הָלַ֖כְתָּ אֶת רֵעֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Hushai said to Absalom, No; whom YHWH, this people, and every man of Israel choose, to him I will belong, and with him I will remain.

familiar.text: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the LORD, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.

modern.text: “Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the LORD, by the people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל אַבְשָׁלֹם֒ לֹ֕א כִּי֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּחַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה וְהָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה וְכָל אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לא אֶהְיֶ֖ה וְאִתּ֥וֹ אֵשֵֽׁב

verses.restored: Again, whom should I serve? Is it not before his son? As I served before your father, so I will be before you.

familiar.text: And again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father’s presence, so will I be in thy presence.

modern.text: Furthermore, whom should I serve if not the son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”

original.text: וְהַשֵּׁנִ֗ית לְמִי֙ אֲנִ֣י אֶֽעֱבֹ֔ד הֲל֖וֹא לִפְנֵ֣י בְנ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָבַ֨דְתִּי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ כֵּ֖ן אֶהְיֶ֥ה לְפָנֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Absalom said to Ahithophel, Give counsel: what shall we do?

familiar.text: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.

modern.text: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל אֲחִיתֹ֑פֶל הָב֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם עֵצָ֖ה מַֽה נַּעֲשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: Ahithophel said to Absalom, Go in to concubines of your father whom he left to guard house. All Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and hands of all with you will become strong.

familiar.text: And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.

modern.text: Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to keep the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל֙ אֶל אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם בּ֚וֹא אֶל פִּלַגְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִנִּ֖יחַ לִשְׁמ֣וֹר הַבָּ֑יִת וְשָׁמַ֤ע כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי נִבְאַ֣שְׁתָּ אֶת אָבִ֔יךָ וְחָ֣זְק֔וּ יְדֵ֖י כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתָּֽךְ

verses.restored: They spread a tent for Absalom upon roof. Absalom went in to concubines of his father before eyes of all Israel.

familiar.text: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

modern.text: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

original.text: וַיַּטּ֧וּ לְאַבְשָׁל֛וֹם הָאֹ֖הֶל עַל הַגָּ֑ג וַיָּבֹ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל פִּֽלַגְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יו לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Counsel of Ahithophel in those days was as when a man inquired at word of Divine. Thus was all counsel of Ahithophel both to David and to Absalom.

familiar.text: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.

modern.text: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.

original.text: וַעֲצַ֣ת אֲחִיתֹ֗פֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאַל בִּדְבַ֣ר הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כֵּ֚ן כָּל עֲצַ֣ת אֲחִיתֹ֔פֶל גַּם לְדָוִ֖ד גַּ֥ם לְאַבְשָׁלֹֽם

translation_notes: Ziba provides valuable supplies during flight, but David accepts his accusation against Mephibosheth without hearing Mephibosheth, checking accessibility barriers, or investigating evidence.
Mephibosheth depends on others to saddle transport. Disability access and servant control are central to whether he could leave Jerusalem.
David immediately transfers the entire estate to Ziba. Emergency judgment under stress still creates dispossession and requires due process.
Shimei combines political protest, accusation, cursing, stones, and dust. His physical aggression is real, but criticism of an anointed ruler is not a capital offense.
Abishai repeatedly proposes beheading critics. David's refusal is necessary restraint, not proof that all Shimei's claims are Divinely dictated.
David's interpretation that YHWH told Shimei to curse is one possible meaning-making response under collapse; it should not teach survivors that abuse is sent by Divine command.
The exhausted group stops and refreshes itself. Rest is not weakness in political crisis.
Hushai's speech is deliberate deception within espionage and civil war. Religious election language can be used strategically by competing regimes.

The ten concubines are sexually seized in public to establish dynastic possession. This is rape and political sexual violence; their consent is absent and their bodies are used as a message between men.
Ahithophel's reputation for oracle-like counsel does not make abusive counsel sacred, infallible, or ethically acceptable.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not dispossess disabled people on a caretaker's accusation, execute critics, or call abuse Divinely commanded. Verses 21-22 describe public rape of ten women as political strategy. Never refer to it as consensual sex, prophecy fulfillment that excuses perpetrators, or a punishment those women carried for David.
